## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` needs a fix before merge: it stores keys without lower-casing them, but `get` always looks up the lower-cased key, so any value set under a mixed-case key can never be read back. This review read `app/cache.py` and `tests/test_cache.py` in full. It traced `set` against the case-insensitivity rule documented at `app/cache.py:14-15` and against the `get` lookup path. It also read the new tests but did not run them. One strength: `test_entries_expire` patches `time.monotonic` on the module that `app/cache.py` calls through, so the expiry check runs on fixed times instead of real clock time.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `Cache.set(key, value)` method and raises `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds, with the comment updated to match. It also adds tests for the set/get round trip, the default TTL value and expiry.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `cache.set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `cache.get("Alpha")` returns `None`, because `set` writes `self._store["Alpha"]` while `get` reads `self._store.get(key.lower())` (`app/cache.py:17`). This breaks the rule documented at `app/cache.py:14-15`: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first, or mixed-case callers create duplicate entries that never expire together." `test_set_then_get_round_trip` only sets the already lower-case key `"alpha"`, so it cannot catch this. — Any caller that sets a key containing upper-case characters gets a cache miss on every read. That entry is also never removed, because `get`'s expiry deletion only runs on the lower-cased key, so these entries stay in `_store` for the life of the cache. — Fix: Write `self._store[key.lower()] = ...`, and add a test that calls `set` with a mixed-case key (for example `"Alpha"`) and then reads it back with `get`.
